articleSummary: Chickenpox, caused by Varicella zoster virus, is rising rapidly during seasonal transitions in Vietnam. Seek care for prolonged high fever, severe lethargy, or purulent lesions; pregnancy or immune compromise require vigilance. articleSummary: Influenza A(H2N2) reemerges as a priority in pandemic preparedness. After decades of absence from humans, waning immunity and animal reservoirs reintroduce risk. A Vaccine study traces the 1957 Asian flu pandemic driven by H2N2, originated in China and displaced by H3N2 in 1968 through genetic reassortment. People born before 1968 retain some immune memory, but most of the world lacks pre-existing H2N2 immunity, though T-cell responses may offer limited protection. Modern vaccine development focuses on platforms, including ferritin nanoparticle vaccines and DNA-based delivery, to minimize exposure to animal reservoirs. The 1957 outbreak caused an estimated 1–4 million deaths. Across about seven decades, at least 25 H2N2 mutations have occurred in humans, with clinical trials showing varying immune responses across populations. Immunity against H2 declined from near 100% in 1968 to about 15.3%, underscoring the need for ready-to-deploy vaccines and stronger pandemic preparedness.

articleHeadline: Zoonotic Disease Prevention at China's Human-Animal Interface
articleSummary: China faces zoonotic disease risk not only from wildlife but from routine activities; a Science in One Health review synthesizing evidence on 93 monitored zoonoses urges prevention at the human–animal–environment interface rather than reactive outbreak response. Four priority interfaces are domestic animals in households/markets; wildlife management in rural settings; rodents and bats in residential environments; and nature-based tourism/cave recreation. High-risk groups include smallholder farmers, herders, rural residents, market vendors, and workers in informal settings; risk varies by animal group and setting. Surveillance gaps cover informal wildlife trade, exotic pets, traditional medicine, and limited behavioral data. Risk communication should be trusted local messengers, participatory formats, livelihood-relevant messaging, and alignment of health with conservation to avoid stigmatization. SARS, H7N9, and COVID-19 illustrate China’s capacity; law updates (April 2025) reinforce prevention under One Health. Upstream steps require stronger intersectoral coordination and data sharing with interface-specific strategies.

articleSummary: Bangladesh is experiencing a severe measles outbreak with 227 children dead since March and about 34,980 suspected cases nationwide as of April 29, 2026. The hardest-hit area is Kurukpata in the Chittagong Hill Tracts near the Myanmar border, a remote region with indigenous communities where vaccination coverage is low and vaccine hesitancy persists. Local health authorities report more than 80 measles cases treated in Kurukpata. Community leaders note unusually high case counts and travel difficulties, with residents, often poor farmers, needing to walk several kilometers to reach a hospital. WHO describes measles as highly contagious via respiratory droplets and capable of serious complications. Bangladesh health agencies, aided by WHO, UNICEF, and security forces, are conducting vaccination campaigns to curb transmission and broaden immunization among indigenous populations.

articleHeadline: Taiwan to resume pork exports to Philippines after regaining ASF-free status: Premier - Focus Taiwan
articleSummary: Taiwan will resume pork exports to the Philippines on May 14 after regaining African swine fever (ASF)-free status with WOAH. Manila notified Taiwan that exports of breeding pigs, pig semen, frozen pork, offal, and pig skin may restart. The Philippines suspended live pigs and pork imports from Taiwan on Dec. 8, 2025 after Taiwan’s first ASF outbreak in October last year at a Taichung farm. The farm was cleaned and disinfected; samples after Nov. 21, 2025 tested negative, and the case was closed and reported to WOAH on Jan. 23, 2026. Taiwan submitted Feb. 21 an application to regain ASF-free self-declared status, which WOAH recognized on Apr. 6. Taiwan had earlier been recognized by WOAH in May last year as ASF-free, making it the first Asian country to attain disease-free status for ASF, FMD and CSF. Singapore said on Apr. 9 it will resume imports from Taiwan.

articleSummary: Brazil's sanitary authority Anvisa recalls batch 13099022444 of frozen Sardine Laje sardines (spined and eviscerated versions) in 800 g packs after laboratory tests detected Salmonella, prompting an immediate nationwide ban on sales and consumption published in the Diário Oficial da União. articleSummary: Chikungunya continues to drive severe illness in Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, with patients reporting intense body pain, high fever, and prolonged fatigue. Eligible groups are 18–59 years with comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes, certain medications such as corticosteroids); pregnant women cannot be vaccinated. Vaccination is offered at Jaguapiru 2 and Bororó 2 Indigenous Units, with plans to extend to May 9 and weekend “Days D” drives. Health teams triage entrants; many patients enter chronic chikungunya, requiring management up to two years.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Avian Influenza and Foreign Trade: Key Insights for Understanding the Impact on the Chilean Industry
articleHeadline: Influenza aviar y comercio exterior: claves para entender el impacto en la industria chilena
articleSummary: Highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreak in Chile highlights the link between animal health and international trade. Confirmation of a outbreak in the Metropolitan Region led Chile to auto-suspend avian exports, triggering immediate trade restrictions by importing countries. Dr. Paula Toro Mujica of the Universidad de O'Higgins notes that global frameworks—the OIE Terrestrial Animal Health Code and the WTO SPS Agreement—guide risk-based measures such as zoning, veterinary certification, and surveillance. The main challenge is rapid outbreak control, preventing spread, and proving absence of viral circulation, requiring public–private coordination, culling, sanitation, movement restrictions, and active surveillance. Biosecurity is essential to prevent virus entry/exit, focusing on isolating birds, controlling people/vehicles/inputs, protecting water and feed sources, and strict cleaning protocols, with staff training and SAG reporting. Economic impacts include potential loss of Chinese imports and logistics disruption; responses should strengthen biosecurity, traceability, and market diversification.

articleSummary: 561 diarrhea cases were recorded in Bengkulu City, Bengkulu Province, Indonesia from January to March 2026, per the City Health Office. If diarrhea occurs, administer oral rehydration solution; zinc supplementation for children for 14 days supports recovery. Prevention through Clean and Healthy Living Behavior (PHBS) is key to reducing cases.

articleHeadline: Nigeria, nine countries account for majority of hepatitis deaths globally - WHO
articleSummary: WHO reports Nigeria and nine other countries accounted for most hepatitis deaths in 2024. Hepatitis B and C caused 1.34 million deaths, with about 1.8 million new infections annually. An estimated 287 million people live with chronic HBV or HCV. HBV has 0.9 million new infections; Africa bears 68% of HBV infections yet only 17% of newborns receive birth-dose vaccination. HCV adds 0.9 million infections; 44% occur among people who inject drugs. Progress includes 32% fewer HBV infections since 2015 and 12% fewer HCV deaths; HBV under-five prevalence is 0.6%, with 85 countries on track for 2030 targets. WHO urges faster vaccination, testing and treatment, safer injections, and stronger primary-care integration; Egypt, Rwanda and the UK cited as progress examples.

articleHeadline: Portable Tuberculosis Diagnostic Tool Matched Traditional Tests' Results
articleSummary: Portable MiniDock MTB TB diagnostic tool, used with sputum or tongue swabs, matched Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and met WHO near-point-of-care targets in a multinational study across seven high-burden countries (India, Nigeria, the Philippines, South Africa, Uganda, Vietnam, Zambia). Among TB cases, sputum-sample sensitivity (MiniDock 86.7%) was comparable to Xpert Ultra (89.4%) and superior to sputum-smear microscopy (62.4%). Non-TB specificity was 97.9% (MiniDock) vs 99.0% (Xpert Ultra) and 99.8% with smear. The WHO targets include ≥85% sputum-sample sensitivity, ≥75% nonsputum sensitivity, ≥98% specificity. Costs under $400; battery-powered; results in 12–25 minutes; no laboratory infrastructure. Tongue swab performance drops in paucibacillary disease (53.4% in smear-negative), underscoring ongoing diagnostic challenges; usability strong (median SUS 75, 17/18 acceptable).

articleSummary: Galloylquinic acids from Copaifera lucens Dwyer leaves, native to Brazil's Atlantic Forest, exhibit multi-target anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity. articleSummary: Porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV), globally endemic for more than a decade, causes severe diarrhea and high mortality in suckling piglets and can infect birds, rodents, ruminants, and humans, challenging swine health and public health. Guangdong Academy of Agricultural Sciences' Institute of Animal Health researchers Zhang Jianfeng and Liu Zhicheng report that the pig-derived GTPase-binding protein 1 (sGBP1) robustly inhibits PDCoV replication via two complementary mechanisms. Second, sGBP1 directly binds viral RNA, preventing the RTC from obtaining a template and blocking transcription and replication. sGBP1 is an interferon-induced NTPase that hydrolyzes GTP to GDP and GMP. The work, funded by national programs, advances understanding of interferon-stimulated antiviral defenses and identifies new targets for anti-coronavirus therapies; online in Journal of Virology.

articleSummary: Ed Sheeran revealed on Instagram from Jakarta that he has been battling herpes zoster (shingles) for about a month and is now recovering as of 30 April 2026. The illness causes a skin rash with fluid-filled blisters and significant pain, typically on one side of the body. Shingles is caused by Varicella Zoster virus (VZV), the same virus that causes chickenpox. After recovery from chickenpox, VZV can remain dormant in nerve tissue and reactivate later as shingles, often in people over 50 or with weakened immunity. Transmission occurs through direct contact with vesicle fluid and can spread via bodily fluids; exposure can also cause chickenpox in someone who has never had it. Treatments include antiviral drugs (acyclovir, famciclovir, valacyclovir), pain relievers (ibuprofen, acetaminophen), corticosteroid injections or local anesthesia, and capsaicin cream after the rash heals.
